title: Canucks sign Zeev Buium to 8-year, $9.38 million AAV contract extension
content:
The Vancouver Canucks have locked up young defender Zeev Buium with a massive second contract, the team announced on Friday.

The contract itself is a whopper, a maximum-term eight-year deal worth $75.04 million ($9.38 million AAV).

Buium, 20, was the signature piece that the Canucks returned in the Quinn Hughes blockbuster trade with the Minnesota Wild in December of 2025. In his first season of NHL action, Buium managed six goals and 26 points while appearing in 76 games with Minnesota and Vancouver in 2025-26.

“Zeev has settled in nicely with our organization since his trade to Vancouver last season, and we are extremely happy to see him make this long-term commitment to the Canucks,” Canucks general manager Ryan Johnson said in the news release. “He is a key member of our young core and a player we will build around moving forward. Zeev has a lot of upside, and we feel with his abilities he will flourish in the system and environment we are creating inside our locker room. We look forward to working together and creating a strong partnership and foundation for our future.”

A storied defender at the NCAA level with Denver University, Buium is a gifted puck mover. While he’s undersized and left-handed, his competitive motor and character stood out significantly to the Canucks over the course of his first season with the club.

Perhaps most importantly from a Canucks perspective, this extension gets in under the wire before the expiry of the current NHL/NHLPA collective bargaining agreement (CBA) on September 15. Under the current rules, an eight-year deal for Buium is permissible, but it won’t be in two weeks.

“We’ve looked and talked about it all summer,” Johnson told The Athletic of considering an extension for Buium prior to the expiry of the current CBA. “If there’s an opportunity to take advantage of a rule while it exists, we’d be crazy not to explore it. There’s nothing I’m not willing to listen on, talk about and if it makes sense for the vision, ultimately do.”

This story will be updated.
